relevance_note: The paper describes identifiable TNFAIP3 heterozygotes, e.g. "a heterozygous TNFAIP3 p.T647P variant in subjects III.1, III.2, and II.2", plus a second family with p.N98Tfs25.
method_note: Read the whole letter, figure legends, Methods and Table E1 manually; rows were typed into a small Python script (no automatic table transcription) and every span was checked verbatim by script. Scope: family 1 (p.T647P) gives III.1 (proband), III.2 and II.2 (carriers), II.4 (pedigree relative, deceased of early-onset SLE, genotype not stated) and II.1 (family member whose sera were tested; genotype and phenotype not stated); family 2 gives the 4-year-old boy (no label in the paper, so 'unnamed person 1') and his heterozygous father. The relationship of II.4 and II.1 to the proband is not stated beyond the pedigree labels. Table E1 has patients as columns; its single data column header is 'Subject III.1 (reference range)'. Inheritance left 'not reported' for III.1, III.2 and the boy: the paper shows the mother (II.2) and the father, respectively, carry the variant and says segregation was ascertained, but never states the variant was inherited from them (rule 8); parental carrier status is recorded in parental_testing_statement. variant_type left 'not reported' because the authors do not name the class. Ethnicity and non-consanguinity are stated for the proband and the boy only and were not copied to relatives. Age 8 years for III.1 is age at presentation (she was followed for >24 months after baricitinib), so it was not recorded as age at last evaluation; no age at diagnosis is given. 'No history of systemic symptoms' (III.1) was recorded as its own excluded feature but not used to exclude checklist items such as recurrent fever. The boy's 'recurrent oral inflammation' was not counted as oral ulcers on the checklist; the father's 'similar clinical features from early childhood' is too vague for feature rows. Table E1 values outside the printed reference ranges (hemoglobin 10 g/L, IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 high, ALP low) were not recorded as features because the authors do not interpret them; the text's garbled sentence lists immunoglobulin levels among apparently negative/normal tests while Table E1 shows IgG and IgA above range (possible inconsistency). Contradictions: the text places the lesions in the paracentral lobule and thalamus 'on the left' (with left-sided seizures and hemiparesis), whereas the Fig 1 legend says 'right paracentral lobule'; laterality was kept only in verbatim detail. Hemoglobin '10 g/L (120-160 g/L)' looks like a unit or typing error. The boy was sequenced on a panel citing reference E1, but the paper does not say he was described there, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null. n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated are null because the authors give no count.
